cf.title: Planner chooses an index-only scan for an index AM without amcanreturn, and execution fails

input.subject: BUG #19638: Planner chooses an index-only scan for an index AM without amcanreturn, and execution fails

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated with a reproducer, including an in-core test module on master (message #3), and the fix is one extra guard in check_index_only() that reuses the existing per-column canreturn flags. The remaining points are a missing regression test and an unsettled list of affected branches, which are not level 1-2 matters. Confidence is medium because the v3 diff and commit message are not shown and no committer has confirmed the analysis.

brief.title: Reject index-only scans when the index AM can return no columns
brief.problem: The planner builds an index-only scan over an index AM that has amoptionalkey = true, amgettuple set and no amcanreturn, and the executor then fails with "no data returned for index-only scan". It affects queries whose target list needs no column of the table, such as count(*), select with an empty list and EXISTS. The report shows the failure on 19beta3 with the third-party diskann AM, and 18.6 plans a disabled seq scan for the same query.
brief.proposed_design: check_index_only() gets one more guard after the bms_is_subset() test, which is true when attrs_used is empty. The first patch rejected the path when index_canreturn_attrs is empty. That also rejected valid index-only scans over expression-only indexes, so v3 checks the per-column canreturn flags inside the existing loop instead.
user_visible_surface: Planner behaviour only: index-only scans are no longer chosen for indexes where no column is returnable.
author_claims: The fix is minimal and touches only check_index_only() in indxpath.c.
The reporter says v3 fixes the reproducer and the select-with-empty-list and EXISTS cases on 18.6.
The reporter says v3 keeps index-only scans for expression indexes and plain column indexes.
make check passes, 231 of 231 tests, on 18.6 with v3.
The same class of problem was fixed in get_actual_variable_range() by 74197bdc842.
brief.thread_state: The reporter and Andrey agree on v3, and the reporter has nothing further. David Rowley first suspected mixed binaries and asked how pgvectorscale was built for 19; he has not replied since the in-core test module was posted.
unclear: The CommitFest record shows only the commit message of the first patch; the v3 commit message and diff summary are not shown.
No patch adds a regression test or a test module, though the reporter says one would be needed.
Message #1 says 18.6 works, but message #4 reports the same errors on 18.6 with the test module, so the affected branches are not settled.
Nobody has bisected whether the path-generation mask commit of 2026-01-28 made the failure easier to hit.
The thread does not say which branches the fix should be back-patched to.

prior_attempts.title: Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
prior_attempts.quote: Moreover, it broke EXPLAIN for such indexquals (which indicates a gap in our test cases :-().
prior_attempts.reason:
Commit 4ace45677 failed to fix the problem fully, because the
same issue of attempting to fetch a non-returnable index column
can occur when rechecking the indexqual after using a lossy index
operator.  Moreover, it broke EXPLAIN for such indexquals (which
indicates a gap in our test cases :-().

Revert the code changes of 4ace45677 in favor of adding a new field
to struct IndexOnlyScan, containing a version of the indexqual that
can be executed against the index-returned tuple without using any
non-returnable columns.  (The restrictions imposed by check_index_only
guarantee this is possible, although we may have to recompute indexed
expressions.)  Support construction of that during setrefs.c
processing by marking IndexOnlyScan.indextlist entries as resjunk
if they can't be returned, rather than removing them entirely.
(We could alternatively require setrefs.c to look up the IndexOptInfo
again, but abusing resjunk this way seems like a reasonably safe way
to avoid needing to do that.)

This solution isn't great from an API-stability standpoint: if there
are any extensions out there that build IndexOnlyScan structs directly,
they'll be broken in the next minor releases.  However, only a very
invasive extension would be likely to do such a thing.  There's no
change in the Path representation, so typical planner extensions
shouldn't have a problem.

As before, back-patch to all supported branches.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 changed how IndexOnlyScan rechecks quals on non-returnable columns. This proposal only closes the empty attrs_used case in check_index_only(). P1's remark about weak test coverage is relevant, because make check did not catch the v1 expression-index regression (message #6).

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The fix enforces the documented index AM contract for third-party AMs without amcanreturn; no struct or callback changes.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: check_index_only() in indxpath.c stops building index-only scan paths for indexes where no column is returnable.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: It is a bug fix, and messages #1 and #4 disagree on whether 18.6 is affected, so the back-patch range is open.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which branches fail with the in-core test module, given that message #1 says 18.6 works and message #4 reports the same errors on 18.6?
Which branches should the fix be back-patched to?
Will the patch add a test module with an AM that has amoptionalkey = true, amgettuple set and no amcanreturn, so the case stays covered?
Does a bisect show that the path-generation mask commit of 2026-01-28 made the failure reachable in the pgvectorscale reproducer?
Can the v3 patch carry an updated commit message that describes the per-column canreturn check and the expression-index case it preserves?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows index path generation in the planner and the index AM API. David Rowley replied in message #2 with a mixed-binaries theory and has not replied since the in-core test module was posted.
committability.liability: A planner check that decides when index-only scans are allowed, back-patched to an unsettled set of branches. A wrong condition would silently remove valid index-only scans, as v1 did for expression-only indexes.
committability.author_follow_up: Good sign: the author produced v3 after the reporter found that v1 rejected valid index-only scans over expression-only indexes.

priority.reason: The failure needs a third-party AM with amoptionalkey = true, amgettuple and no amcanreturn, but it is a core planner bug that produces an unexecutable plan. The patch touches one function in indxpath.c, and reporter and author agree on v3, so it now waits for a committer.

provisional_note: The v3 diff and commit message were not shown, so the exact condition and its effect on indexes with a mix of returnable and non-returnable columns could not be checked. The claim that v3 keeps expression-index and plain-column index-only scans rests on the reporter's tests alone.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Use tuple-level SIREAD locks for index-only scans
precedents_retrieved.summary: Index-only scans that skip the heap would take tuple-level SIREAD locks instead of locking the whole heap page, with a fix to the outdated comment in nodeIndexonlyscan.c. A later experimental patch also skipped the btree page lock when the scan uses equality quals on all key columns of a unique index.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying after a collision in the test files, and Daniel Gustafsson asked for a rebased version. No new version appears in the visible messages, so the entry was returned with feedback. Earlier, David Rowley found that deferrable unique constraints broke the btree lock skip, and Thomas Munro fixed that case in v4. Thomas Munro was still unsure the fix covered every case.

precedents_retrieved.title: Index Only Scan for index expressions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch extends the planner so that index-only scans can be used when a query's target list or restriction clauses contain expressions that exactly match index expression columns, not only plain attribute columns. Matching requires the expression tree (or a subtree) to be identical to the index expression; no normalization of commutative or associative operators is attempted.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Testing of the sixth patch version by Vladimir Sitnikov found an error ("variable not found in subplan target list") when queries access non-indexed columns alongside an expression index. Robert Haas marked the entry Returned with Feedback because these bugs precluded committing it before the CommitFest ended, while inviting resubmission and saying the effort was good.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix buffer pinning logic/visibility bugs in [SP-]Gist Index-Only Scans
precedents_retrieved.authors: Peter Geoghegan (pgeoghegan), Michail Nikolaev (nkey), Matthias van de Meent (mmeent), Mihail Nikalayeu (mihailnikalayeu)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a race in GiST and SP-GiST index-only scans, where concurrent VACUUM can remove a TID and set the visibility map bit before the scan checks it, so a dead tuple is returned. Later versions drop the idea of holding pins on index pages: they add a table AM API (table_index_vischeck_tuples) so the index AM checks the visibility map while it still holds the page pin, and they also change nbtree to use it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last visible message (v14, December 2025) only fixes a CFBot failure, and the entry was withdrawn about six months later with no visible objection or explanation. The author had moved a backpatchable version of the fix to a separate thread.

precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a GiST fetch function for the cube extension so that queries on cube columns can use Index Only Scans. It reuses g_cube_decompress() as the fetch function, since both only need to detoast the key.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it as obsolete after commit d3a4f89 (Allow no-op GiST support functions to be omitted). He said he would work on a broader patch for contrib modules to support GiST Index Only Scans and remove no-op support functions.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support SK_SEARCHNULL / SK_SEARCHNOTNULL for heap-only scans
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes heap scans honor SK_SEARCHNULL and SK_SEARCHNOTNULL scan keys in HeapKeyTest(), which skey.h documents as supported only for index scans. The goal was convenience for extensions that scan tables directly without SPI; a later follow-up by Jacob Champion added planner pushdown of IS [NOT] NULL quals into Seq Scan as scan keys.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas saw no benefit in heapam support alone and asked that nodeSeqScan.c use it, with performance results, and that the table AM API get an 'amsearchnulls' field. The author wanted to defer the executor part to a later patch, so Heikki marked the entry Returned with Feedback. The later executor and planner patches got no visible review before the entry closed.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add parallel columns for seq scan and index scan on pg_stat_all_tables and _indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds parallel_seq_scan, last_parallel_seq_scan, parallel_idx_scan and last_parallel_idx_scan columns to pg_stat_all_tables, and parallel_idx_scan and last_parallel_idx_scan to pg_stat_all_indexes. The goal is to help administrators judge how parallel workers are used and tune parallelism settings.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers doubted that per-table and per-index counts of parallel scans help with tuning, since parallel plans with Gather nodes are usually analyzed per statement. Michael Paquier added that the metrics committed in e7a9496de906 and 5d4298e75f25 may already cover the need. Robert Haas found no clear use case for these counters. The author agreed that the committed metrics were good enough for now.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think the question to which we don't have a clear answer is: for what purpose would you want to be able to distinguish parallel and non-parallel scans on a per-table basis?

precedents_retrieved.title: introduce optimized linear search functions that return index of matching element
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds SIMD linear search functions, pg_lfind8_idx() and pg_lfind8_ge_idx(), that return the index of the first matching byte instead of true/false. It came from the radix tree work for lazy vacuum dead tuple storage, and this version also reworks the simd.h helpers it uses.
precedents_retrieved.objection: John Naylor judged that this level of abstraction is not right for the intended use case, the radix tree for lazy vacuum. He said some of the low-level simd.h improvements would be used later in that work, and he returned the entry with feedback.

As I mentioned in the radix tree thread, I don't believe this level of

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
Reverted commit(s): Ignore BRIN indexes when checking for HOT udpates; Move test for BRIN HOT behavior to stats.sql
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits 5753d4ee32 and fe60b67250 that modified HOT to
ignore BRIN indexes. The commit message for 5753d4ee32 claims that:

    When determining whether an index update may be skipped by using
    HOT, we can ignore attributes indexed only by BRIN indexes. There
    are no index pointers to individual tuples in BRIN, and the page
    range summary will be updated anyway as it relies on visibility
    info.

This is partially incorrect - it's true BRIN indexes don't point to
individual tuples, so HOT chains are not an issue, but the visibitlity
info is not sufficient to keep the index up to date. This can easily
result in corrupted indexes, as demonstrated in the hackers thread.

This does not mean relaxing the HOT restrictions for BRIN is a lost
cause, but it needs to handle the two aspects (allowing HOT chains and
updating the page range summaries) as separate. But that requires a
major changes, and it's too late for that in the current dev cycle.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return historic snapshot during LR
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return historic snapshot during LR
Reverted commit(s): Don't allow GetTransactionSnapshot() in logical decoding
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 1585ff7387 changed GetTransactionSnapshot() to throw an error
if it's called during logical decoding, instead of returning the
historic snapshot. I made that change for extra protection, because a
historic snapshot can only be used to access catalog tables while
GetTransactionSnapshot() is usually called when you're executing
arbitrary queries. You might get very subtle visibility problems if
you tried to use the historic snapshot for arbitrary queries.

There's no built-in code in PostgreSQL that calls
GetTransactionSnapshot() during logical decoding, but it turns out
that the pglogical extension does just that, to evaluate row filter
expressions. You would get weird results if the row filter runs
arbitrary queries, but it is sane as long as you don't access any
non-catalog tables. Even though there are no checks to enforce that in
pglogical, a typical row filter expression does not access any tables
and works fine. Accessing tables marked with the user_catalog_table =
true option is also OK.

To fix pglogical with row filters, and any other extensions that might
do similar things, revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return a
historic snapshot during logical decoding.

To try to still catch the unsafe usage of historic snapshots, add
checks in heap_beginscan() and index_beginscan() to complain if you
try to use a historic snapshot to scan a non-catalog table. We're very
close to the version 18 release however, so add those new checks only
in master.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent records a reason that applies here. P1 is a different fix in the same area, and its reason does not hit v3, because any qual column makes attrs_used non-empty and the existing subset test rejects the path. P3 concerned bugs in a different feature, so it is not listed. The thread cites one earlier discussion, the get_actual_variable_range() check (messages #1 and #3), and describes it as a fix for the same assumption in another place, not as a rejection.

The change affects only queries that fail today with "no data returned for index-only scan", and v3 keeps index-only scans for expression and plain column indexes (messages #6 and #8). It adds no syntax, GUC, catalog or dump change, so a back-patched plan change has no working query to break.

The fix changes only the path test in check_index_only(). It reads the existing IndexOptInfo canreturn flags and adds no on-disk, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or struct change. Plans are not persistent, so standbys, pg_upgrade and back-patching across minor releases are unaffected, and extensions see no ABI change.

The proposal only stops the planner from building index-only scan paths it cannot execute. No privilege, role, visibility rule, RLS policy or new information channel is added, and an unprivileged user gains nothing new, so the security angle finds no objection.

No maintenance or fit objection. v3 adds one flag inside an existing per-index loop in check_index_only(), so planning cost is unchanged, there is no new API, GUC or catalog state, and the fix closes a gap in the documented index AM contract. Not checked without the code: the missing regression test module is a level 4 matter, and a committer has not engaged since message #2.

From the already-exists angle there is nothing to raise. This is a planner bug fix, and no existing feature, setting or extension stops the planner from choosing an index-only scan over an index AM that cannot return columns. v3 reuses the existing per-column canreturn[] flags filled from index_can_return() and adds no second mechanism.

Demand is shown. The planner builds an unexecutable plan for an index AM configuration that the AM API allows, and the diskann AM in pgvectorscale, a third-party extension in real use, exposes it through count(*), select with an empty target list and EXISTS. The extension cannot work around this, because an amcanreturn that always returns false leaves the planner in the same state as a NULL one.
